newsitem.title: UK: Prompt North Sea premiums lose more ground.
newsitem.headline: Prompt North Sea premiums lose more ground.

text.p: Prompt Norwegian North Sea physical grades lost more ground on Monday despite better refining margins and better prospects for U.S. sales.
But Dated Brent appeared to have bottomed and intermonth spreads widened with a higher outright market.
Poor refinery demand and a stubborn overhang of prompt cargoes forced sales of Norwegian Ekofisk and Statfjord for late September and early October at substantially lower numbers.
Ekofisk moved at Dated Brent plus 13-15 cents, Statfjord at plus 10 cents.
"It looks as if this overhang is just being rolled forward rather than wiped out," said a trader. "It doesn't look too good for October at this point."
Dated Brent, having sold at a Nov -47 cents discount was looking in slightly better shape as a U.S. trader booked a million barrel tanker for the U.S. Gulf.
"The arb looks close to open again, so that should help things," said a trader.
Brent for Sept 23-25 and Sept 25-27 loading was offered at Oct -40 cents, about Nov +12 cents.
CFDs for next week were traded at a steady Nov Brent +20-21 cents.
Prompt Oct/Nov Brent moved higher to +50 cents as November recovered some of Monday's losses.
One of two Brent cargoes nominated loading dates on Tuesday was left unclaimed at the five o'clock deadline, traders said.
An October 2-4 loader was left clocked with trading house Cargill. BP kept a second October 2-4 cargo.
